doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Current plans and his computer tools
summary: He teaches, plays in the Bill Bell Trio, plans an organ trio, and uses Performa and Encore on his computer.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well actually I mean see another thing about this area, you can always re-invent yourself. Now I’ve been teaching a lot this past couple of years so I haven’t really been playing out nights. There’s a couple of groups I play with, one is the Bill Bell Trio. It’s the Eddie Marshall Trio when it’s my job and it’s Bill Bell — and that’s sounding like a straight ahead jazz trio. But I’m trying to put together an organ trio with organ, saxophone and drums. And that will probably be my next adventure. And plus writing for this ensemble, which that’s going to take a lot of my time.
Are you able to hear things back when you do the computer?
Oh, well I am hooked up. I’ve got every modern gadget.

You know the thing is, when I was in high school, I went to a technical high school, took a technical course, it was electronics and carpentry and all of this sort of stuff. That’s why I had my business. And so I bought a computer maybe like ten years ago, after swearing I would never use a computer. But ten years ago I bought a computer and I bought Performa, which is a sequencing program, and Encore, which is a music writing program, and a lot of manuals. And I sort of like mastered all of it, because I’m pretty clever at mastering stuff. So I have it now and I can play my music on the computer and it writes it out and I have scores and it looks pretty neat you know. And I’m always learning new programs. So really I am into the computer. Not that I do music for presentation but it’s my tool at this point.
Great. Well you’ve come a long way since you hitchhiked from Lenox, Mass. That’s a great story.
